Nicola Costa’s stage manager’s desk and locker (with the branch chief’s approval):

· In the desk drawer, under the pencils, line 14’s safety pin; luminous tape on its ring and fibres from a thin leather glove.

STAGE MANAGER’S DESK — SEARCH
It was recorded that the safety pin was found in the drawer of Nicola Costa’s desk.
The pin wasn’t on the stage.
The flyman said he put the pin in every evening, and the pin was found in the drawer.
The death was deemed an accident; the flyman retired.
Amedeo Pace was arrested and, after thirty-five years, dismissed from the theatre; the drawer was never opened.
Nicola Costa was arrested. Caruso Marittima’s double-bottomed tour crates were reported to the Tokyo branch.
Sofia Marchetti was arrested; the tour crates went back to the port.

Aurelio was going to open the crate. Don’t ask what was in the crates; I only said which crate went on which lorry, and the Carusos’ man said thank you. I sent Amedeo away, put my glove on, pulled the pin, released the lock. I put the pin in my desk drawer. I write everything down so the curtain goes up on time; I wrote that down too, then rubbed it out.
You pulled 14’s pin.
At the stage manager’s desk, where I always am. Amedeo forgot to put 14’s pin in; he’s getting old, I warned him how many times.

I sent Amedeo to the back door for a lorry; I must have been given the wrong message. I never left my desk.

On the evening of 9 October 2030, during the dress rehearsal of ‘Tosca’ at the Teatro Partenope, the baritone Aurelio Mancini (54) was killed when a twenty-five-kilo sandbag fell on him from the fly system.

On stage and in the wings during the rehearsal: stage manager Nicola Costa, flyman Amedeo Pace, soprano Sofia Marchetti, costume designer Chiara Fontana. The guest conductor Kenji Arai was leading the orchestra. The doorkeeper Pasquale Vitale was at the stage door.
INCIDENT REPORT
Request the cue book and headset log
Request permission to search the stage manager’s desk
Request an examination of the rigging system

· The lock on rope line 14 is open; its safety pin is missing.
· Without the pin, the lock can be released over the rope with a single blow of the hand; the sandbag reaches the stage in about two seconds.
· Line 14 is never used in the second act; in that act only the baritone stands at centre stage.
· On the rope, the marks of a thin glove, not the flyman’s.
RIGGING SYSTEM EXAMINATION
Soprano.
I protect my voice; the rest doesn’t concern me.

It ended a year ago. Everyone knows about our fights, because I don’t hide my fights even on stage. But at that moment I was on stage, facing him. If the bag had fallen, it could have fallen on me too. Whoever it was could have killed me as well.
She gathers her cloak on her shoulder.
What was there between you and Aurelio?
Sofia Marchetti — interview

The conductor heard the order on the headset, but if he wasn’t spoken to before the rigging examination, he went back to Tokyo. The doorkeeper said there was no lorry; the costume designer described the double-bottomed crate. The cue book’s rubbed-out line and the headset log opened a justified search; the pin was in the drawer.
The curtain went up on time. Everything was written down; only one line had been rubbed out.
Teatro Partenope — October 2030

Stage manager Nicola Costa knew which of the Caruso Marittima crates carrying the theatre’s touring sets had double bottoms. When the baritone Aurelio Mancini decided to open a crate, Costa sent the flyman to the back door at the dress rehearsal with a false report of a lorry, put on his glove, pulled line 14’s pin and released the lock.
Who killed Aurelio Mancini?
